nodes.label: analyze.js
nodes.summary: Song analysis: cut a film to a song you did not write. Tempo, beats, downbeats (bars), sections, a per-bar energy curve, strong hits and LRC lyrics, from any audio file (ffmpeg decodes it). node engine/render.js analyze assets/song.mp3 [--lrc assets/song.lrc] [--bpm 128] [--meter 3] → out/analysis.json, beats.js (for score.js: bars, sections, lyrics) and out/analysis.svg (a picture to check) score

nodes.label: dsp.js
nodes.summary: Tiny DSP toolkit — everything the soundtrack needs, written from scratch.

nodes.label: genres.js
nodes.summary: Genre packs: a whole backing track (drums, bass, chords) in one call, in a style. const Genre = require('./engine/audio/genres'); Genre.play('lofi', { clock, from: 0, to: 8, chordAt: sc.chordAt, buses: { drums, bass, pad, keys } }); Styles: lofi · chiptune · orchestral · edm · afrobeats · qawwali · desi (dholak pop) · boombap. Each one: a tempo range to pick from, swing, a 16-step drum grid per in

nodes.label: instruments.js
nodes.summary: Instruments: each function renders ONE note/hit into a mono Float32Array.

nodes.label: mix.js
nodes.summary: Mixing + mastering helpers: sidechain pump, gates, master bus, WAV writer.

nodes.label: sing.js
nodes.summary: Sing: short sung lines (jingles, a name in "Happy Birthday", a chant) from spelled syllables. A formant singer: a glottal source at the note's pitch through five vowel formants (the classic soprano/alto/tenor/bass tables), consonants made of noise bursts, hisses, hums and glides. Consonants start just before the note so the vowel lands on the beat, like a real singer. const Sing = require('./engin

nodes.label: voice.js
nodes.summary: Voiceover: offline text-to-speech, placed on the timeline, with word timings (for captions) and a mouth envelope (for lip-sync). Runs inside song.js, synchronously. const Voice = require('./engine/audio/voice'); const vo = Voice.speak([ { at: T(1), text: 'Meet Pantrio.', voice: 'Samantha' }, { at: T(3), text: 'It plans your week of meals in ten seconds.', who: 'mum' }, ], { out: path.join(__dirnam

nodes.label: geo.js
nodes.summary: Map data for engine/video/data.js (load it before data.js when a film draws maps). Country outlines: Natural Earth (public domain) via world-atlas 2.0.2 (ISC), outer rings only, simplified. world: 1:110m for every country; detail: 1:50m for Pakistan and its region. Borders follow Natural Earth's de facto lines; draw your own when a film needs a different view. Rings are flat [lon, lat, lon, lat, …

nodes.label: music.js
nodes.summary: Musical time + pitch helpers shared by the score, the synth and the visuals. Works in Node (require) and in the browser (globalThis.MUSIC).

nodes.summary: Subtitles / burned-in captions: one list, drawn word by word in the film AND exported as .srt/.vtt. Many people watch muted, and platforms read caption text for search, so every film should have them. score.js: subtitles: [{ t, end, text, alt?, words?: [{ w, t }] }] - words (optional): word times (the voiceover writes its estimates into out/voice.json); otherwise the line's time is shared out by w

nodes.label: brand.js
nodes.summary: Brand kit tools. node engine/render.js brand -> checks brand.json and draws out/brand.png (colours, fonts, logo, CTA, claims) node engine/render.js brand-from <url> -> reads a real website and writes a draft brand.json (+ assets/logo.*, assets/fonts/*) brand.json: { name, tagline, url, colors: { primary, secondary, ink, bg, muted, surface, onPrimary, success }, fonts: { display: { family, file, we

nodes.label: formats.js
nodes.summary: node engine/render.js formats 16:9,9:16[,1:1,4:5] [workers] [--draft | --res 1440] -> out/<name>-16x9.mp4, out/<name>-9x16.mp4 … : one score, every format, each verified and muxed. Works for films that lay themselves out (score.js uses `const FORMAT = U.pickFormat('…')` and film.js draws from G.W / G.H / G.SAFE). The music is shared: run node song.js once before.

nodes.label: levels.js
nodes.summary: "Ears" for a model that can't listen: RMS / peak (dBFS) of each WAV, per section of the film. Run from the project root: node engine/tools/levels.js out/music.wav out/stem-*.wav Sections come from SCORE.S ({ name: [t0, t1] }) if present, otherwise 8 equal slices.

nodes.label: pacing.js
nodes.summary: node engine/render.js pacing [name] -> the hook and pacing report of the final film + out/pacing.svg Short-form platforms measure how many viewers get past the first 3 seconds, and retention research recommends a "pattern interrupt" (a cut, a big change) every 10–15 seconds. This measures both on the rendered file: picture change per frame, sound level, cuts, and on-screen text from the score.

nodes.label: plan.js
nodes.summary: node engine/render.js plan -> out/plan.md: a one-page treatment of the film, generated from score.js, for the user to approve BEFORE the full render (and to re-check after changes): format and length, a bar map of sections with their events, the named moments, every word the film shows (a checklist of claims to verify), the cast and the brand rules.

nodes.label: poster.js
nodes.summary: node engine/render.js poster [@t …] [--title "Price?"] [--sub "Show the price"] -> out/poster-1..3.png (1280x720 YouTube thumbnails, three layouts for Test & Compare), out/posters.png (all three side by side) and, for tall films, out/cover.png (1080x1920 Reels/TikTok cover). What wins clicks (thumbnail CTR studies): one dominant subject, high contrast, ≤ 5 words of bold text that still reads when

nodes.label: snap.js
nodes.summary: node engine/render.js snap <url> [--desktop] [--full] [--out assets/site.png] [--hide ".cookie-banner,#popup"] [--dark] [--wait 1500] A real screenshot of a website, as a phone (390×844 at 2x) or a desktop (1440×900) sees it, for UI.imageScreen (a screenshot scrolling inside UI.phone) or a Ken Burns pan (G.kenBurns). --full the whole page (scrolls first so lazy images load; capped at 12 screens) -

nodes.label: srt.js
nodes.summary: node engine/render.js srt -> out/<name>.srt and out/<name>.vtt for uploading to YouTube / TikTok / Instagram. Source, in order: the voiceover's word timings (out/voice.json), score.js `subtitles`, score.js `captions`.

nodes.label: util.js
nodes.summary: Shared math helpers: deterministic randomness, noise, easing. Everything here is pure so audio + video workers stay perfectly in sync.

nodes.label: boot.js
nodes.summary: The frame contract between a film and the renderer. A film calls Studio.film({ draw(ctx, t) { ... } }) and the renderer calls window.renderAt(t, fmt, scale).

nodes.label: chars.js
nodes.summary: Characters: Claude (the little orange block), a customizable person, footballers, a ball.

nodes.label: data.js
nodes.summary: Data on screen: numbers that count up on the beat, bar / line / donut charts, and maps with pins and routes (pins dropping across Pakistan, a flight from Lahore to London). Everything is a pure function of t, drawn with the hand-drawn toolkit (so it follows the film's style pack). index.html: <script src="engine/data/geo.js"></script> (maps only) then <script src="engine/video/data.js"></script> D

nodes.label: gfx.js
nodes.summary: Hand-drawn graphics toolkit: boiling pencil lines, hatching, torn paper, tape, text.

nodes.label: player.js
nodes.summary: Live preview WITH SOUND: plays out/music.wav and draws the film at the audio clock, so timing can be judged by eye and ear before a full render. Opened by `node engine/render.js preview` (a local page on a random port; the renderer injects this script into index.html). Keys: space play/pause · ←/→ one beat (shift: one bar) · [ ] previous/next marker · L loop the section under the playhead · Home b

nodes.label: shots.js
nodes.summary: Shots, transitions and camera: write a film as a list of shots instead of an if/else chain. const film = Shots.film([ { at: 0, draw: intro }, { at: T(4), draw: verse, cam: Shots.push(1, 1.08) }, { at: T(8), draw: drop, in: 'flash', cam: Shots.shake(14, T(8)) }, { at: T(12), draw: outro, in: { type: 'iris', color: '#F2B84B', at: [960, 540] } }, ]); Studio.film({ draw: film }); Each shot's draw(ctx,

nodes.label: ui.js
nodes.summary: Product / brand UI kit: crisp app screens inside the hand-drawn world (phone mockup, cards, pills, buttons, chat, stats, progress, wipes). Text uses the system UI font like real apps do; colours come from UI.theme, so a film can wear any brand: UI.setTheme({ accent: '#…' }). Every function is a pure function of its arguments (and t), like the rest of the engine.

nodes.label: film-lib.js
nodes.summary: Shared pieces for the film: the cast, the world (sky, sea, sand, cliff, town), props (plane, kite, board, keypad, phone) and the LENS: the magnifier that opens on a far-away detail.

nodes.label: film.js
nodes.summary: THE FILM: 28 scenes, one per block of the script, each a pure function of t. Scene and line times come from score.js (the measured voiceover); the lens pops are the same events the song plays tings on.

nodes.label: lines.js
nodes.summary: THE SCRIPT, one spoken line per entry, grouped by scene. Prefix = speaker (no prefix = the narrator): F friend · K teacher · B Mr. Black · G Grandpa Sam · T Theo · N Nova. A line ending in "..." gets a longer held pause after it. timing.js turns this into timeline.js using the real voice durations.

nodes.label: score.js
nodes.summary: WHAT IF YOUR EYESIGHT WAS 100x SHARPER? (16:9, ~6 min). The voiceover's measured line times (timeline.js, from timing.js) are the spine: every scene, lens pop, hit and music section is placed from them, so the voice, the picture and the score cannot drift apart.

nodes.label: song.js
nodes.summary: THE SONG: a narrated film, so the music is a bed under the voice. Every sound comes from score.js: one clock (84 BPM), one chord table, mood runs per scene, a glassy ting on every lens pop, and hits on the scene cuts. The music ducks under the voice. node song.js (STEMS=1 writes stems)

nodes.label: 1. beach
nodes.summary: You look up from the beach. A plane crosses the sky. You can read the name on its tail.

nodes.label: 2. moon
nodes.summary: You glance at the Moon. Craters. Mountains. Shadows. No telescope.

nodes.label: 3. hill
nodes.summary: A friend points at a hill two kilometers away. What's that? You squint.

nodes.label: 4. plate
nodes.summary: Your name is Theo. A British driving test asks you to read a number plate... from twenty meters.

nodes.label: 5. acuity
nodes.summary: Normal eyes pick out details about one sixtieth of a degree wide. Yours? A hundred times finer.

nodes.label: 6. rule
nodes.summary: But here's the rule. Your eyes got a hundred times sharper. Your legs did not.

nodes.label: 7. title
nodes.summary: So what if your eyesight was a hundred times sharper?

nodes.label: 8. class
nodes.summary: Plus: you never need glasses. From the back row, you can read the teacher's notes on her desk. Do you?

nodes.label: 9. stadium
nodes.summary: At the football match, you sit in the cheapest seat in the stadium. You can still read the stitching on the ball.

nodes.label: 10. birds
nodes.summary: In birdwatching club, everyone shares binoculars. You count the feathers... out loud.

nodes.label: 11. fovea
nodes.summary: The catch? Your sharpest vision only lives in one tiny spot. Hold your thumb out at arm's length.

nodes.label: 12. harbor
nodes.summary: But where it gets really crazy... is the video. A tourist films you at the harbor.

nodes.label: 13. message
nodes.summary: By Friday, a message. Mr. Black. Polite.

nodes.label: 14. cost
nodes.summary: And there's a cost. You can't switch it off. Peeling paint.

nodes.label: 15. grandpa
nodes.summary: Then there's Grandpa Sam. He used to be a lifeguard on this beach. Now he has macular degeneration.

nodes.label: 16. cliff
nodes.summary: Every Sunday, you climb the cliff together. He flies his big red kite. It's the one thing he still finds...

nodes.label: 17. roof
nodes.summary: Sunday comes. But you're not on the cliff. You're on a café roof, two kilometers down the coast.

nodes.label: 18. sea
nodes.summary: Then... you see it. Far out past the beach.

nodes.label: 19. choice
nodes.summary: Theo? The numbers. Now. You can see the PIN.

nodes.label: 20. call
nodes.summary: You drop the earpiece. If I can see it... it's mine to fix.

nodes.label: 21. kite
nodes.summary: The red kite climbs. Left, Grandpa. More. Stop. Hold it there.

nodes.label: 22. nova
nodes.summary: You call the lifeguard station. Her name is Nova. Follow the red kite.

nodes.label: 23. saved
nodes.summary: Three minutes later, the boy is coughing on the sand. Alive... and furious about his board.

nodes.label: 24. police
nodes.summary: And Mr. Black? You never gave him a single number. You gave the police something better.

nodes.label: 25. sunset
nodes.summary: That evening, you're back on the cliff. Grandpa grips your shoulder. Tell me what you see.

nodes.label: 26. real
nodes.summary: Is any of this real? Partly. Macular degeneration is real, and it steals central vision first.

nodes.label: 27. sting
nodes.summary: That night, you look up at the Moon. And something on its surface... moves.

nodes.label: 28. cta
nodes.summary: So would you trade normal eyes for pizza-sized ones? What do you think? Tell us in the comments, and tell us which superpower we should do next.

nodes.label: 1. spider
nodes.summary: A spider drops onto your hand. You don't scream. You just...

nodes.label: 2. haunted
nodes.summary: The lights die in the haunted house. A monster leaps from the dark. Everyone shrieks.

nodes.label: 3. coaster
nodes.summary: Your roller coaster creeps to the top of the first drop. The whole car is screaming. You?

nodes.label: 4. brain
nodes.summary: Your name is Sam. Deep in your brain sit two tiny clusters shaped like almonds. Together they're called the amygdala.

nodes.label: 5. sm
nodes.summary: This isn't pure fantasy. Scientists studied a real woman known only as S.M. A rare disease damaged both her amygdalae.

nodes.label: 6. rule
nodes.summary: But here's your rule. Your fear is gone. Your danger is not.

nodes.label: 7. title
nodes.summary: So what if you had zero fear? And what's life actually like without it?

nodes.label: 8. speech
nodes.summary: Monday. A speech in front of the whole school. Five hundred faces.

nodes.label: 9. space
nodes.summary: Minus: personal space. Most people stand roughly an arm's length from a stranger. You?

nodes.label: 10. zoo
nodes.summary: At the zoo, you walk straight to the reptile house. The keeper lets you hold the python. Then begs you to stop.

nodes.label: 11. skate
nodes.summary: The catch? Your body still breaks. You try the biggest ramp at the skate park.

nodes.label: 12. bridge
nodes.summary: But where it gets really crazy... is the glass bridge. Hundreds of meters above a valley.

nodes.label: 13. message
nodes.summary: Then a message arrives. Mr. Black. He runs the biggest stunt channel online.

nodes.label: 14. cost
nodes.summary: And there's a cost. A roller coaster is fun for a reason. Your body screams danger.

nodes.label: 15. faces
nodes.summary: And the worst part? The amygdala doesn't only make fear. It helps you spot fear in other faces.

nodes.label: 16. leo
nodes.summary: Then there's Leo. Your best friend since you were six. Leo is scared of everything.

nodes.label: 17. tell
nodes.summary: When you tell him about Mr. Black, he goes quiet. You can't read his face, of course. But he taps.

nodes.label: 18. crane
nodes.summary: You go anyway. An old crane at the docks. A steel beam, forty meters up.

nodes.label: 19. ladder
nodes.summary: Then the ladder rattles. Leo? He followed you.

nodes.label: 20. choice
nodes.summary: You look at his face. You can't read it. To you, it's just...

nodes.label: 21. rescue
nodes.summary: You turn around. You don't rush. You can't feel it...

nodes.label: 22. truth
nodes.summary: At the bottom, he collapses in the dust. Then you pick up the camera Mr. Black dropped. Still live.

nodes.label: 23. lesson
nodes.summary: And remember: no video is worth a hospital bed. If someone asks you to drop your safety gear for views...

nodes.label: 24. brave
nodes.summary: The comments fill with one name. Leo. Leo, who climbed thirty meters while terrified.

nodes.label: 25. end
nodes.summary: Later he asks how you stayed so calm. You shrug. I can't feel it. So I have to think it.

nodes.label: 26. sting
nodes.summary: That night, an envelope slides under your door. No stamp. No name.

nodes.label: 27. cta
nodes.summary: So what would you do with zero fear? Tell us the first scary thing you'd try in the comments. And if you got chills when Leo tapped twice...
